note.explanation: Laboratory safety is a shared responsibility. Learn the warning signs, follow instructions, use protective equipment, and know what to do in an emergency. Keep chemicals labelled and handle hazardous substances only as instructed.
examples: Add acid to water, never water to acid.
Carry out reactions that produce harmful gases in a fume cupboard.
note.checkAnswer: Add acid to water; never add water to acid.
note.simple: Be careful with chemicals, read their labels, and know how to respond to danger.
note.checkQuestion: When diluting an acid, which should be added to which?
note.title: Laboratory safety and hazards
steps: Read labels and warning signs before handling chemicals.
Follow safety instructions and wear suitable protective equipment.
Keep flames, sparks, and sudden shocks away from hazardous chemicals.
Use a fume cupboard for reactions that may release harmful gases.
In an emergency, alert others, follow the emergency plan, and get help.

options: the responsibility of the students only
the responsibility of the professor only
the responsibility of the lab. incharge only
mcqs.stem:
Q13.1. Safety in the chemistry laboratory is:
(a) the responsibility of the students only
(b) the responsibility of the professor only
(c) the responsibility of the lab. incharge only
(d) a shared responsibility
rationales: This is wrong because laboratory safety is not only the students' responsibility.
This is wrong because laboratory safety is not only the professor's responsibility.
This is wrong because laboratory safety is not only the lab incharge's responsibility.
This is correct because everyone in the laboratory shares responsibility for safety.

mcqs.stem:
Q13.2. Accidents often result from:
(a) making mistakes
(b) failure to use common sense
(c) failure to follow instructions
(d) all of the above
rationales: This can cause accidents, but it is not the only listed cause.
This can cause accidents, but it is not the only listed cause.
This can cause accidents, but it is not the only listed cause.
This is correct because each of the listed behaviours can lead to accidents.

options: that the chemical can cause less serious injury
that the chemical can cause serious injury
that user should be careful when using chemical
that user should open it only in the presence of a teacher
mcqs.stem:
Q13.3. The label “Warning” on a chemical bottle signifies:
(a) that the chemical can cause less serious injury
(b) that the chemical can cause serious injury
(c) that user should be careful when using chemical
(d) that user should open it only in the presence of a teacher
rationales: This does not state the general caution meant by the warning label.
This is not the meaning given for the warning label in this question.
This is correct because a warning label tells the user to be careful when using the chemical.
This is not what the label itself signifies.

options: that the material is an oxidizing agent
that the material can degrade rapidly upon exposure
that its contact destroys living tissue
mcqs.stem:
Q13.4. The label “Corrosive” on a chemical bottle indicates:
(a) that the material is an oxidizing agent
(b) that the material can degrade rapidly upon exposure
(c) that its contact destroys living tissue
(d) that the chemical can explode
rationales: An oxidizing agent is a different hazard category.
Rapid degradation is not the meaning of the corrosive label.
This is correct because corrosive substances can destroy living tissue on contact.
Explosive is a different hazard from corrosive.

mcqs.stem:
Q13.5. Example of highly toxic chemical:
(a) Ethanol
(b) Acetic acid
(c) Potassium cyanide
(d) Potassium permanganate
rationales: Ethanol is not the highly toxic example identified here.
Acetic acid is not the highly toxic example identified here.
This is correct because potassium cyanide is a highly toxic chemical.
Potassium permanganate is not the highly toxic example identified here.

mcqs.stem:
Q13.6. Example of self-reactive chemical:
(a) Potassium
(b) Phenol
(c) Picric acid
(d) n-Hexane
rationales: Potassium is reactive, but it is not the self-reactive example identified here.
Phenol is not the self-reactive example identified here.
This is correct because picric acid is identified as a self-reactive chemical.
n-Hexane is not the self-reactive example identified here.

mcqs.stem:
Q13.7. When diluting an acid with water:
(a) do it quickly
(b) do not stir the container
(c) always add acid to water
(d) always add water to acid
rationales: Diluting acid quickly is not the safe instruction.
This is not the safe instruction for diluting acid.
This is correct because adding acid to water helps reduce the danger from heat and splashing.
This is wrong because adding water to concentrated acid can cause dangerous splashing.

options: close gas valves and turn off all equipments
carry chemicals out of the lab.
mcqs.stem:
Q13.8. What should you do in case of a fire drill in the lab.?
(a) run to safety shower
(b) climb into the fume cupboard
(c) close gas valves and turn off all equipments
(d) carry chemicals out of the lab.
rationales: A safety shower is for certain contamination emergencies, not the action specified for a fire drill.
A fume cupboard is not a place to shelter during a fire drill.
This is correct because closing gas valves and switching off equipment helps reduce further danger when safe to do so.
Carrying chemicals out creates unnecessary risk during a fire drill.

written.finalAnswer: Examples include concentrated sulphuric acid, hydrochloric acid, nitric acid and sodium hydroxide.

rubric.why: Identifying corrosive acids shows recognition of this hazard class.
rubric.description: Names suitable corrosive chemicals.
rubric.how: Give one or more examples such as concentrated sulphuric, hydrochloric or nitric acid.

rubric.why: A further valid example completes the response.
rubric.description: Gives another corrosive example.
rubric.how: Name another corrosive chemical, such as sodium hydroxide.

modelAnswer: Examples of corrosive chemicals include concentrated sulphuric acid, hydrochloric acid and nitric acid.
Sodium hydroxide is another example.

written.text: Q13.2. What type of safety precautions are adopted to avoid damage due to explosive chemicals?
written.finalAnswer: Keep explosive chemicals away from heat, flames, sparks, friction and sudden shock; handle and store them carefully according to instructions.

rubric.why: Explosives may be triggered by heat or ignition sources.
rubric.description: Keeps explosives away from heat and ignition.
rubric.how: State that they must be kept away from heat, flames or sparks.

rubric.why: Impact and careless handling can trigger some explosive substances.
rubric.description: Prevents impact and handles chemicals carefully.
rubric.how: Mention avoiding sudden shock or friction and following handling instructions.

modelAnswer: Keep explosive chemicals away from heat, flames and sparks.
Avoid friction and sudden shock; handle and store them carefully according to instructions.

written.text: Q13.3. What type of damages can reactive chemicals cause?
written.finalAnswer: Reactive chemicals may react violently, cause fires or explosions, release harmful gases, and damage skin, eyes or property.

rubric.why: Violent reactions can cause immediate physical damage.
rubric.description: Identifies violent reactions, fires or explosions.
rubric.how: State at least one physical danger caused by reactive chemicals.

rubric.why: Reactive chemicals can also harm people through fumes or contact.
rubric.description: Identifies injury or harmful gas release.
rubric.how: Mention harmful gases or damage to people or property.

modelAnswer: Reactive chemicals may react violently and cause fires or explosions.
They may release harmful gases and damage skin, eyes or property.

written.text: Q13.4. Indicate two such safety instructions which are required to avoid radiation.
written.finalAnswer: Limit exposure time and keep as far as possible from the radiation source; use suitable shielding and follow warning signs.

rubric.why: Reducing exposure time reduces the radiation received.
rubric.description: Limits time near a radiation source.
rubric.how: State that exposure time should be kept as short as possible.

rubric.why: Distance and shielding reduce exposure and safe procedures prevent accidental contact.
rubric.description: Uses distance, shielding or required warnings.
rubric.how: Give another precaution such as increasing distance or using suitable shielding.

modelAnswer: Keep exposure time as short as possible.
Keep a safe distance from the source and use suitable shielding.

written.text: Q13.5. Which chemicals can cause suffocation?
written.finalAnswer: Asphyxiant chemicals, including gases that displace oxygen, can cause suffocation.

rubric.why: The term asphyxiant identifies chemicals that can cause suffocation.
rubric.description: Names the hazard category.
rubric.how: State that asphyxiant chemicals can cause suffocation.

rubric.why: Explaining oxygen displacement or giving an example supports the identification.
rubric.description: Explains how suffocation can occur or gives an example.
rubric.how: Mention gases that reduce available oxygen or give a suitable gas example.

modelAnswer: Asphyxiant chemicals can cause suffocation.
Some gases do this by displacing oxygen in the air.

written.text: Q13.6. Why signs and symbols are posted on lab. and chemical bottles?
written.finalAnswer: They warn people about hazards and give information needed to handle and store chemicals safely, helping to prevent accidents.

rubric.why: Recognising a hazard before use helps prevent exposure and accidents.
rubric.description: States that signs and symbols warn of hazards.
rubric.how: Explain that they show the danger associated with the laboratory or chemical.

rubric.why: The warning helps users choose safe handling and storage actions.
rubric.description: Connects the warning to safe practice.
rubric.how: Say that signs guide safe use and help prevent accidents.

modelAnswer: Signs and symbols warn people about the hazards in the laboratory and on chemical bottles.
They help users handle and store chemicals safely and prevent accidents.

written.text: Q13.7. How fire caused by chemicals should be handled?
written.finalAnswer: Raise the alarm, alert the teacher or lab incharge, and use the correct fire-fighting method only if it is safe; evacuate and follow emergency instructions.

rubric.why: Promptly alerting others allows a safe and coordinated response.
rubric.description: Raises the alarm and gets help.
rubric.how: State that the teacher or lab incharge must be alerted immediately.

rubric.why: Correct response and evacuation reduce the chance of injury.
rubric.description: Uses suitable fire response or evacuates safely.
rubric.how: Mention a suitable method only when safe, then follow emergency instructions.

modelAnswer: Raise the alarm and alert the teacher or lab incharge immediately.
Use the correct fire-fighting method only if it is safe; otherwise evacuate and follow emergency instructions.

written.text: Q13.8. Why emergency drills are important to face emergency situations?
written.finalAnswer: Emergency drills teach people what to do, where to go and how to act quickly and calmly, reducing confusion and injury during a real emergency.

rubric.why: Practice helps people remember the correct actions.
rubric.description: Explains that drills prepare people.
rubric.how: State that drills teach or practise emergency procedures.

rubric.why: A practised response can reduce panic, confusion and harm.
rubric.description: Explains how drills improve the response.
rubric.how: Mention acting calmly or reducing confusion and injury.

modelAnswer: Emergency drills teach people what to do and where to go in an emergency.
They help people act quickly and calmly, reducing confusion and injury.

written.text: Q13.1. How will you handle an emergency situation caused by fire due to short circuiting?
written.finalAnswer: Raise the alarm, alert the teacher or lab incharge, switch off the electricity only if safe, do not use water on an electrical fire, and evacuate using the safe route.

rubric.why: An immediate warning brings help and protects others.
rubric.description: Raises the alarm and alerts the responsible person.
rubric.how: State that the alarm should be raised and the teacher or lab incharge informed.

rubric.why: Disconnecting power, if safe, helps stop the electrical source.
rubric.description: Deals safely with the electrical supply.
rubric.how: Say to switch off electricity only if it can be done safely.

rubric.why: Water can conduct electricity and make the situation more dangerous.
rubric.description: Avoids putting water on an electrical fire.
rubric.how: Explicitly state not to use water on the fire.

rubric.why: Moving away from danger is essential if the fire cannot be safely controlled.
rubric.description: Evacuates safely or identifies an appropriate response.
rubric.how: State that people should evacuate by a safe route and follow instructions.

modelAnswer: Raise the alarm and alert the teacher or lab incharge.
Switch off the electrical supply only if it is safe to do so.
Do not use water on an electrical fire.
Evacuate by the safe route and follow emergency instructions.

written.text: Q13.2. What type of reactions should be carried out in fume cupboard?
written.finalAnswer: Reactions that produce toxic, poisonous, irritating or otherwise harmful gases and vapours should be carried out in a fume cupboard.

rubric.why: A fume cupboard helps protect people from harmful substances in the air.
rubric.description: Identifies reactions producing hazardous fumes.
rubric.how: Mention reactions that give off toxic or harmful gases.

rubric.why: The answer must connect the hazardous emissions to the correct equipment.
rubric.description: Names gases or vapours and the fume cupboard.
rubric.how: State that such reactions are carried out in a fume cupboard.

modelAnswer: Reactions that produce toxic, poisonous, irritating or otherwise harmful gases and vapours should be carried out in a fume cupboard.

written.text: Q13.3. Put forward at least two suggestions to improve safety in the lab.
written.finalAnswer: Follow the laboratory instructions and wear suitable protective equipment; keep chemicals labelled and know the emergency procedures.

rubric.why: Following instructions and using protective equipment reduce exposure and accidents.
rubric.description: Gives a valid personal safety measure.
rubric.how: Name one measure such as following instructions or wearing goggles.

rubric.why: A second practical measure further improves safe laboratory practice.
rubric.description: Gives another valid safety suggestion.
rubric.how: Name a different measure, such as keeping labels clear or learning emergency procedures.

modelAnswer: Follow laboratory instructions and wear suitable protective equipment.
Keep chemicals properly labelled and learn the emergency procedures.

written.text: Q13.4. Can you identify warning symbols posted for radiation and asphyxiant chemicals?
written.finalAnswer: Radiation is indicated by the radiation trefoil symbol; an asphyxiant warning identifies a substance that can cause suffocation, often by displacing oxygen.

rubric.why: The radiation trefoil warns that a radiation hazard is present.
rubric.description: Identifies the radiation warning symbol.
rubric.how: Name or describe the radiation trefoil warning.

rubric.why: The asphyxiant warning indicates a suffocation risk.
rubric.description: Identifies the asphyxiant warning.
rubric.how: Explain that the symbol warns of a substance that can cause suffocation.

modelAnswer: The radiation warning is the radiation trefoil symbol.
The asphyxiant warning indicates a chemical that can cause suffocation, for example by displacing oxygen.

written.text: Q13.5. Why sudden shock can cause some chemicals to explode?
written.finalAnswer: Some unstable or shock-sensitive chemicals can be triggered by an impact; the sudden energy starts a rapid reaction that releases heat and gases, causing an explosion.

rubric.why: Sensitivity explains why impact can initiate a reaction.
rubric.description: Identifies that some chemicals are unstable or shock-sensitive.
rubric.how: State that shock-sensitive chemicals can be triggered by impact.

rubric.why: A rapid energy-releasing reaction explains the resulting explosion.
rubric.description: Explains how the shock leads to an explosion.
rubric.how: Mention a rapid reaction that releases heat or gases.

modelAnswer: Some unstable chemicals are sensitive to sudden shock or impact.
The impact can start a rapid reaction that releases heat and gases, causing an explosion.

written.text: Q13.1. Explain hazards due to explosive and toxic chemicals.
written.finalAnswer: Explosive chemicals may detonate when exposed to heat, flames, sparks, friction or shock, causing blast injuries, burns and damage. Toxic chemicals can poison people by inhalation, swallowing or skin contact; toxic gases can cause serious illness or death.

rubric.why: The trigger and explosive nature of the hazard must be explained.
rubric.description: Explains how explosive chemicals may be triggered.
rubric.how: Mention triggers such as heat, sparks, friction or shock.

rubric.why: Describing the consequences shows the danger of an explosion.
rubric.description: Gives effects of an explosion.
rubric.how: State that explosions can injure people or damage property.

rubric.why: Toxic chemicals can enter the body by several routes.
rubric.description: Explains how toxic substances affect people.
rubric.how: Mention poisoning through inhalation, swallowing or contact.

rubric.why: The severity of toxic exposure must be recognised.
rubric.description: States a serious effect of toxic exposure.
rubric.how: Mention serious illness or death, especially from toxic gases.

modelAnswer: Explosive chemicals may detonate when exposed to heat, flames, sparks, friction or sudden shock.
The blast may cause injuries and burns and damage laboratory equipment or buildings.
Toxic chemicals can poison people if inhaled, swallowed or absorbed through the skin.
Toxic gases may cause serious illness or death.

written.text: Q13.2. Write down five such common safety instructions which are used to avoid all types of hazards.
written.finalAnswer: Read labels and follow instructions; wear suitable protective equipment; never taste chemicals and avoid direct contact; keep the laboratory tidy and chemicals properly stored; report accidents and know the emergency procedures.

rubric.why: Knowing the hazard and required procedure prevents unsafe handling.
rubric.description: Reads labels and follows instructions.
rubric.how: Include a clear instruction about labels, signs or directions.

rubric.why: Protective equipment reduces exposure to chemical hazards.
rubric.description: Uses suitable protective equipment.
rubric.how: Name a suitable item or say to wear protective equipment.

rubric.why: Avoiding ingestion, inhalation and contact helps prevent poisoning and injury.
rubric.description: Avoids unsafe exposure to chemicals.
rubric.how: State a suitable rule such as never tasting chemicals or avoiding direct contact.

rubric.why: A safe workspace and emergency readiness help prevent and manage accidents.
rubric.description: Gives a further common safety instruction.
rubric.how: Mention tidy storage, reporting accidents or learning emergency procedures.

modelAnswer: Read chemical labels and follow the teacher's instructions.
Wear suitable protective equipment, such as goggles and a lab coat.
Never taste chemicals and avoid direct contact with them.
Keep the laboratory tidy and store chemicals safely.
Report accidents immediately and learn the emergency procedures.

written.text: Q13.3. Explain the importance of warning signs and symbols to avoid any accident in the lab.
written.finalAnswer: Warning signs and symbols quickly identify hazards such as corrosive, toxic, explosive, radiation and asphyxiant dangers. They help users choose suitable precautions, handle and store substances correctly, and avoid accidents.

rubric.why: Signs are useful because they make hazards recognisable before use.
rubric.description: Explains that signs identify or warn about hazards.
rubric.how: State that warning signs show the type of danger.

rubric.why: Examples demonstrate understanding of the hazards communicated.
rubric.description: Gives examples of hazards shown by signs.
rubric.how: Name one or more hazard categories.

rubric.why: Warnings guide the user towards safer handling and storage.
rubric.description: Explains how signs guide safe action.
rubric.how: Link the warning to precautions or safe chemical use.

rubric.why: The final purpose is preventing harm and accidents.
rubric.description: States the safety benefit.
rubric.how: Explain that understanding signs helps prevent accidents or injury.

modelAnswer: Warning signs and symbols identify hazards before a person handles a chemical or enters a hazardous area.
They show dangers such as corrosive, toxic, explosive, radiation or asphyxiant hazards.
This information helps users choose suitable precautions and handle and store chemicals correctly.
Understanding the signs helps prevent accidents and injury.

written.text: Q13.4. Name some toxic chemicals. Describe the effects of spreading toxic gas in the lab.
written.finalAnswer: Examples of toxic chemicals include potassium cyanide, chlorine and phenol. Toxic gas spreading in a laboratory can be inhaled, causing poisoning, breathing difficulty, serious illness or death; it may also affect people before they can escape.

rubric.why: Examples show recognition of toxic chemicals.
rubric.description: Names toxic chemicals.
rubric.how: Give suitable examples such as potassium cyanide or chlorine.

rubric.why: The hazard is specifically the spread and inhalation of toxic gas.
rubric.description: Explains exposure to the gas.
rubric.how: State that the gas can spread through the laboratory and be inhaled.

rubric.why: The answer should describe the effects on health.
rubric.description: Gives health effects of toxic gas exposure.
rubric.how: Mention poisoning, breathing difficulty or serious illness.

rubric.why: Toxic gas can be fatal and make evacuation urgent.
rubric.description: Recognises the severe danger.
rubric.how: State that exposure can be fatal or requires immediate evacuation.

modelAnswer: Examples of toxic chemicals include potassium cyanide, chlorine and phenol.
A toxic gas can spread through the laboratory and be inhaled by people.
It can cause poisoning, breathing difficulty and serious illness.
Severe exposure may cause death, so people must be warned and evacuated promptly.

written.text: Q13.5. A student has spilled over a corrosive and explosive chemical due to an accident. Which emergency measures you will take to tackle the situation.
written.finalAnswer: Warn others and alert the teacher or lab incharge; keep people away and avoid touching or cleaning the spill yourself. Remove ignition sources only if safe, follow the chemical's emergency instructions, and evacuate if needed. Get trained personnel to manage the spill and use the appropriate emergency equipment.

rubric.why: A spill involving corrosive and explosive hazards requires immediate help.
rubric.description: Raises the alarm and informs the responsible person.
rubric.how: State that others are warned and the teacher or lab incharge is alerted.

rubric.why: Keeping people away reduces exposure and injury risk.
rubric.description: Protects people from the spill.
rubric.how: Keep people away or evacuate the affected area.

rubric.why: Untrained cleanup can cause chemical burns or trigger an explosion.
rubric.description: Avoids unsafe handling and leaves cleanup to trained personnel.
rubric.how: Do not touch the spill; get trained people to manage it.

rubric.why: Removing ignition sources, when safe, reduces the risk of explosion.
rubric.description: Controls ignition risk safely.
rubric.how: Mention keeping heat, flames or sparks away, without approaching danger.

rubric.why: Following the emergency plan ensures that the spill is dealt with appropriately.
rubric.description: Follows the spill response and uses suitable help or equipment.
rubric.how: Follow the chemical-specific instructions and use appropriate trained response.

modelAnswer: Warn everyone nearby and alert the teacher or lab incharge immediately.
Keep people away from the spill and evacuate the affected area if necessary.
Do not touch or attempt to clean the corrosive and explosive chemical yourself.
Keep heat, flames and sparks away; remove ignition sources only if this can be done safely.
Follow the chemical's emergency instructions and have trained personnel manage the spill using suitable equipment.

written.text: Q13.1. A few decades ago, a tanker carrying poisonous chlorine gas leaked and the gas spread over a large area in Lahore. The accident killed a few persons as well as animals. Give some concrete proposals to avoid such an accident in future.
written.finalAnswer: Inspect and maintain tankers, valves and containers; use approved, leak-proof equipment and secure loads; train drivers and handlers; choose safe routes and follow transport regulations; use chlorine leak detectors and emergency plans, with prompt public warnings and evacuation procedures.

rubric.why: Regular inspection and maintenance help prevent leaks.
rubric.description: Prevents equipment failure.
rubric.how: Propose checking and maintaining tankers, valves and containers.

rubric.why: Safe containment and regulated transport reduce the risk of a release.
rubric.description: Improves safe transport and containment.
rubric.how: Mention approved containers, secured loads or transport rules.

rubric.why: Trained workers are more likely to handle hazardous gas safely.
rubric.description: Provides training for responsible people.
rubric.how: Recommend training drivers and chemical handlers.

rubric.why: Early leak detection can limit the spread and speed up response.
rubric.description: Provides early detection.
rubric.how: Suggest gas detectors or checks for leaks.

rubric.why: A planned warning and evacuation can protect people if prevention fails.
rubric.description: Plans for the consequences of an accident.
rubric.how: Include an emergency plan, public warning or evacuation procedure.

modelAnswer: Inspect and maintain tankers, valves and containers regularly, and use approved leak-proof equipment.
Secure the load properly and follow regulations for transporting poisonous gases.
Train drivers and handlers in safe handling and emergency procedures.
Use chlorine gas detectors and inspect for leaks during transport.
Prepare emergency plans that provide prompt public warnings and evacuation if a leak occurs.

examTips: Short-answer questions commonly ask for examples of hazards or two safety precautions; give the required number clearly.
Constructed-response questions often ask what to do in a particular emergency; present actions in a safe, logical order.
Descriptive questions earn marks for both explaining the hazard and stating its effects or precautions.
For warning symbols, name the hazard and explain what action the warning helps the user take.
For spill and gas-leak questions, include warning people, getting responsible help, keeping clear, and following the emergency plan.

steps.why: The responsible person needs to know immediately so they can coordinate help.
steps.text: Raise the alarm and alert the teacher or lab incharge.

steps.why: Removing the electrical supply can reduce the danger, but approaching an unsafe switch may put you at risk.
steps.text: Switch off the electrical supply only if it is safe to do so.

steps.why: Water can conduct electricity and may cause electric shock.
steps.text: Do not use water on an electrical fire.

steps.why: Leaving by a safe route protects people from fire and smoke.
steps.text: Evacuate by the safe route and follow emergency instructions.

example.question: How will you handle an emergency situation caused by fire due to short circuiting?
example.answer: Raise the alarm, alert the teacher or lab incharge, switch off the electricity only if safe, do not use water on an electrical fire, and evacuate using the safe route.

explain.title: Laboratory safety is shared
explain.body: Everyone in the laboratory has a role in preventing accidents. Follow instructions, use common sense and tell the responsible person about hazards.

explain.title: Recognise chemical hazards
explain.body: Corrosive chemicals can destroy living tissue on contact. Toxic chemicals can poison people. Explosive and shock-sensitive substances can cause blasts, while asphyxiants can cause suffocation.

explain.title: Use warning signs and safe procedures
explain.body: Signs and bottle labels warn users about hazards and help them choose the correct precautions. Read labels before handling chemicals and keep chemicals properly stored.

explain.title: Control exposure
explain.body: Carry out reactions that produce harmful gases or vapours in a fume cupboard. Follow specific precautions for hazards such as radiation, and avoid contact with chemicals.

explain.title: Respond safely to emergencies
explain.body: Raise the alarm, alert the teacher or lab incharge, keep people away from danger and follow the emergency plan. Do not attempt a dangerous cleanup yourself.

mistakes: Adding water to concentrated acid instead of adding acid to water.
Ignoring warning signs or handling an unfamiliar chemical without reading its label.
Trying to touch or clean up a hazardous spill without training or instructions.
Using water on an electrical fire.
Forgetting to explain both the hazard and its effects when answering a descriptive question.
